In the temple, Jesus watches a widow give all that she has. People in the crowd note how little she gives. They ask for her to give more. 

But Jesus proclaims to everyone that the widow gave more than everyone else. Everyone else who contributed gave out of the extra money they had. But the widow, even in her poverty, gave everything she owned.
items.description_short: In the temple, Jesus watches a widow give all that she has. People in the crowd note how little she gives. They ask for her to give more.

items.title: Annas Questions Jesuss Authority
items.description:
A Pharisee named Annas asks Jesus what right He has to say the kinds of things he says. In return, Jesus asks Annas a question.

Jesus asks whether John's right to baptize came from God or from man. Annas turns with other Pharisees and talks to them.

So they go back to Jesus and answer that they don't know who gave John the right to baptize. Jesus stares back. He says since they don't know, he won't tell them who gave Him the authority to teach the things He's been teaching.
items.description_short: A Pharisee named Annas asks Jesus what right He has to say the kinds of things he says. In return, Jesus asks Annas a question.

items.title: Parable Of The Vineyard And Tenants
items.description:
Jesus tells the story of a man who plants a vineyard. That man leases the vineyard to workers or tenants.

Jesus shares the verse that the stone the builders rejected would become the most important one. He goes on to state that anyone who falls on that stone will be broken. And if that stone falls on anyone, it will crush that person.
items.description_short: Jesus tells the story of a man who plants a vineyard. That man leases the vineyard to workers or tenants.

items.title: Paying Taxes To Caesar
items.description:
The Pharisees tell Jesus they know He teaches right things. They say Jesus doesn't pay attention to anyone's status. But that Jesus teaches the truth about God's will for all people. And then they ask about paying taxes.

The Pharisee asks Jesus whether or not it's right that they pay taxes to Caesar. Jesus asks the Pharisees to show him a silver coin.
items.description_short: The Pharisees tell Jesus they know He teaches righteous things. But, they also say Jesus doesn't pay attention to anyone elses status. But that Jesus teaches the truth about God's will for all people. And then they ask about paying taxes.

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description:
Passover is about to begin. Jesus sends Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal. Jesus sits with them and looks at all of them. He tells them how glad He is to share the meal before he suffers.

Jesus takes his cup and prays to God. As when He prayed over the bread and fish, He thanks God for the blessing of the fruit of the vine that God brings forth. He passes it to the nearest disciple and tells them all to drink it.

Jesus reaches for a piece of bread and prays again. He thanks God for bringing bread from the earth and breaks it. He passes the two pieces to the disciples and claims that the bread represents His body that's given for them. They should eat and remember Him. The cup is still being passed around. Jesus says that the cup of wine is a new testament in His blood and it's shed for them.
items.description_short: Passover is about to begin. Jesus sends Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal. Jesus sits with them and looks at all of them. He tells them how glad He is to share the meal before he suffers.

items.title: Upper Room Teaching
items.description:
Jesus sits after sharing the bread and wine, sealing a new covenant with His followers, and revealing that there is a traitor among them. He passes on one last specific teaching to His disciples. The disciples listen solemnly.

He tells them that the greatest of them must be like the least of them. And the leader must be like the servant. He asks which one is actually greater: the one who sits down at the table or the one who serves? He says that the one who sits is greater. But then He points out that He Himself came as one who serves.
items.description_short: Jesus sits after sharing the bread and wine, sealing a new covenant with His followers, and revealing that there is a traitor among them. He passes on one last specific teaching to His disciples. The disciples listen solemnly.

items.title: Jesus Is Betrayed And Arrested
items.description:
The council of the Jewish elders meets to see how they can get rid of Jesus. Meanwhile, Jesus sits with the rest of His followers and tells them to pray against temptation.

Judas arrives at the council and counts out his pieces of silver. Jesus walks off alone so that He can pray. He asks His Heavenly Father to take the burden of His cup away from Him. But He says He'd rather have God's will than His own be done. As Jesus continues to pray, His sweat became like great drops of blood. He rises from prayer and returns to the disciples. But they're asleep.

 A crowd of Jews approaches Him. Judas leads the way and gets close to Jesus. He kisses Him on the cheek. The disciples lunge forward asking if they should go to battle. Peter runs forward and cuts the ear off one of the men. Jesus heals the man and stops the brawl. He asks why they come with clubs. And Jesus is arrested.
items.description_short: The council of the Jewish elders meet to see how they can get rid of Jesus. Meanwhile, Jesus sits with the rest of His followers and tells them to pray against temptation.

items.title: Peter Disowns Jesus
items.description:
Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest and guarded by temple guards. They push Him and take His clothing in the courtyard. Peter watches from close by.

Peter is recognized, but denies that He knows Jesus. As dawn approaches, a rooster crows. Jesus looks over to Peter. Peter walks away, undone by his denials.
items.description_short: Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest and guarded by temple guards. They push Him and take His clothing in the courtyard. Peter watches from close by.

items.title: Jesus Is Mocked And Questioned
items.description:
Jesus gets beaten by the temple guards. A man tells the guards to bring Jesus in to see the council.

Annas and Caiaphas enter. The room is full of other Jewish men. They want to know if Jesus is the Messiah. Jesus only replies that if He tells them, the council won't believe Him. He says the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of God.

They ask if He is the Son of God. Jesus replies that they say He is. They don't know what to make of His answer. One of them stands and acts as a witness. Everyone heard His replies. The council decides to take Him to Pilate.
items.description_short: Jesus gets beaten by the temple guards. A man tells the guards to bring Jesus in to see the council.

items.title: Jesus Is Brought To Pilate
items.description:
Roman guards open the gates and take Jesus. They march through the courtyard followed by the crowd. Pontius Pilate marches out. He's known as the most vicious Roman governor, responsible for the crucifixion of thousands.

Pilate demands to know what they want. The Jewish crowd yells that Jesus is confusing their people and that Jesus upset the temple market. They demand a sentence from Pilate.

Pilate asks Jesus if he is the King of the Jews. Jesus only replies, "So you say.&quot
items.description_short: Roman guards open the gates and take Jesus. They march through the courtyard followed by the crowd. Pontius Pilate, the most vicious Roman governor who is responsible for the crucifixion of thousands, come to address the crowd.

items.title: Jesus Is Brought To Herod
items.description:
Jesus is escorted into Herod's presence. Herod looks Him up and down then asks, "Who is it that you say you are?" Jesus remains silent. 

Herod says that he's heard that Jesus can perform miracles and signs. Herod demands that Jesus do something for him. But Jesus stays silent and unmoving.
items.description_short: Jesus is escorted into Herod's presence. Herod looks Him up and down then asks, "Who is it that you say you are?" Jesus remains silent.

items.title: Jesus Is Sentenced
items.description:
Jesus is dragged from Herod's palace. Jesus and the crowds come back to Pilate's courtyard. 

He sits in the judgment seat and says he will only order that Jesus be scourged. The council speaks up again. They remind Pilate that he is supposed to release one man to the Jews during the Passover Festival.

The guards tie Jesus to a pole in the center of the courtyard and start to whip Him with cat o' nine tails that rip the flesh from His back. Pilate watches the courtyard warily before he leaves.

Pilate makes his way back with a scroll. Jesus is released and dragged back in front of Pilate. He drops the crucifixion judgment at Jesus's feet.
items.description_short: Jesus is dragged from Herod's palace. Jesus and the crowds come back to Pilate's courtyard.

items.title: Jesus Carries His Cross
items.description:
Jesus carries His own cross beam through the streets. The Roman guards beat back those in their path. Jesus continues to struggle under the weight of the beam.

He collapses in the street, falling to His knees. A Roman guard looks over the crowd and sees a big man. He is forced to carry the beam while Jesus stumbles along. The crowds yell angrily. But some mourn.

Jesus urges them to weep for themselves because there are harder times coming. The Romans push Jesus along after them, prodding Him forward when He stops or stumbles.
items.description_short: Jesus struggles to carry His own cross beam through the streets, while the Roman guards beat those out of the way in their path. Jesus continues to struggle under the weight of the beam.

items.title: Jesus Is Crucified
items.description:
They arrive at the place where the crosses are being set up. Others are being tied to their crosses. Jesus is stripped and led to His own cross. They throw Him down on it. There are cries as the others are nailed to their crosses.

The nails are hammered through Jesus's wrists and feet as He screams. Then slowly, the crosses are erected as Romans pulls the ropes. Jesus is lifted high in the air. He hangs on the cross, tired and in pain. He prays for those in the crowd. He asks God to forgive them because they don't know what they do.

The crowd murmurs at the feet of the cross. Annas and Caiaphas comment that He saved others. They wonder why He doesn't save Himself. The crowd starts to jeer. They urge Him to save Himself. But He doesn't.
items.description_short: They arrive at the place where the crosses are being set up. Others are being tied to their crosses. Jesus is stripped and led to His own cross. They throw Him down on it. There are cries as the others are nailed to their crosses.

items.title: Soldiers Gamble For Jesuss Clothes
items.description:
As Jesus continues to hang on the cross, the crowd watches in silence. The Roman guards gather around the cross and watch Jesus.

A Roman claims that the clothing is no regular garment. He tosses it to the group of guards. They yell and debate who will get it. One suggests they play, or gamble, for it.
items.description_short: As Jesus continues to hang on the cross, the crowd watches in silence. The Roman guards gather around the cross and watch Jesus.

items.title: Sign On The Cross
items.description:
The Roman guard takes a sign and hammers it above Jesus's head. The crowd erupts with laughing and yelling. The guard tries to give Him vinegar from a sponge.

The guard insists He save Himself if He's really King of the Jews. The crowd continues to yell. But there are a few who look on and cry.
items.description_short: The Roman guard hammers a sign of mockery above Jesus's head. The crowd erupts with laughing and yelling. Then, the guard tries to give Him vinegar from a sponge.

items.title: Crucified Convicts
items.description:
Jesus hangs between two other men. His disciples watch, helpless. One of the men on a cross asks if Jesus is the Messiah. He tells Him to save Himself and them.

The other man on a cross tells him that Jesus receives the same sentence as those who are guilty. But He did nothing wrong. The man asks Jesus to remember him when he comes back as King. Jesus promises the man that he will be in paradise with Jesus.
items.description_short: Jesus hangs between two other men. His disciples watch, helpless. One of the men on a cross asks if Jesus is the Messiah. He tells Him to save Himself and them.

items.title: Death Of Jesus
items.description:
Jesus continues to hang on the cross. Darkness comes over everything. The veil in the temple is torn right down the middle. 

Jesus breathes heavily. He prays and gives up His spirit willingly into the Father’s hand. And then He dies.
items.description_short: Jesus continues to hang on the cross. Darkness comes over everything. The veil in the temple is torn right down the middle.

items.title: Burial Of Jesus
items.description: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pontius Pilate for permission to bury Jesus in a tomb. He receives permission. He and a servant carry the body into the tomb and lay it down on a rocky shelf. Joseph covers the exposed, bloody foot of Jesus and sprinkles dirt on Him.
items.description_short: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pontius Pilate for permission to bury Jesus in a tomb.

items.title: Angels At The Tomb
items.description:
The sun rises the Sunday after the Sabbath. The women return with spices they had prepared. But when they get close, they see the rock has been moved.

Jesus's body is gone. The linens He was wrapped in still lay there, though. Two angels appear and the women bow. They ask why the women look for someone living in the place of the dead. The angels state that Jesus has risen.
items.description_short: The sun rises the Sunday after the Sabbath. The women return with spices they had prepared. But when they get close, they see the rock has been moved.

items.title: The Tomb Is Empty
items.description:
Mary Magdalene rushes into a room full of disciples. She tells the men the stone has been rolled away. And that when she and the others went into the tomb, the body was gone.

Joanna speaks of the angels. She says there were two shining men. And they told the women not to look for the living among the dead.

Peter rushes away and to the tomb. He runs in and walks right to the rocky shelf. But there's no body. There's only the linen. He kneels and takes it in his hands. He shuffles it, looking through it. But after a moment he stops. He sighs and bows his head.
items.description_short: Mary Magdalene rushes into a room full of disciples. She tells the men the stone has been rolled away. And that when she and the others went into the tomb, the body was gone.

items.title: Resurrected Jesus Appears
items.description:
John and others return to the room where Jesus's followers have gathered. They come in saying that Jesus has indeed risen. John says Jesus appeared to Simon on the road. Simon talks about how they didn't recognize Jesus at first.

But when they sat down to dinner and Jesus broke the bread, they knew who He was.

Jesus stands in the room with them. He asks why they're troubled and doubtful. He holds out His hands for them to see. He encourages them to touch Him to prove to them that He's flesh and blood. They reach out and touch His hands.
items.description_short: John and others return to the room where Jesus' followers have gathered. They come in saying that Jesus has indeed risen! John says that Jesus appeared to Simon on the road. Simon talks about how they did not recognize Jesus at first.

items.title: Great Commission And Ascension
items.description:
The men and women follow Jesus down a hill. He says all power has been given to Him in heaven and on earth. So the followers are to go and teach the nations.

He tells them to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He says to teach people how to do everything He taught them. And that He will be with them always.
items.description_short: The men and women follow Jesus down a hill. He says all power has been given to Him in heaven and on earth. So the followers are to go and teach the nations.

items.title: Invitation To Know Jesus Personally
items.description:
A narrator gives an invitation to know God personally.

The invitation is open to everyone. It means turning to God and trusting Jesus with our lives and to forgive our sins. We can speak to Him in prayer when we're ready to become followers of Jesus.
items.description_short: A narrator gives an invitation to know God personally.

original.title: JESUS
original.film_description:
This film is a perfect introduction to Jesus through the Gospel of Luke. Jesus constantly surprises and confounds people, from His miraculous birth to His rise from the grave. Follow His life through excerpts from the Book of Luke, all the miracles, the teachings, and the passion. 

God creates everything and loves mankind. But mankind disobeys God. God and mankind are separated, but God loves mankind so much, He arranges redemption for mankind. He sends his Son Jesus to be a perfect sacrifice to make amends for us.

Before Jesus arrives, God prepares mankind. Prophets speak of the birth, the life, and the death of Jesus.

Jesus attracts attention. He teaches in parables no one really understands, gives sight to the blind, and helps those who no one sees as worth helping.

He scares the Jewish leaders, they see him as a threat. So they arrange, through Judas the traitor and their Roman oppressors, for the crucifixion of Jesus. They think the matter is settled. But the women who serve Jesus discover an empty tomb. The disciples panic. When Jesus appears, they doubt He's real. But it's what He proclaimed all along: He is their perfect sacrifice, their Savior, victor over death. He ascends to heaven, telling His followers to tell others about Him and His teachings.

original.title: Story of Jesus for Children
original.shortDescription: In the first century, a group of children meet together to talk about what they've seen and heard about Jesus. Some believe Jesus is the Son of God. But others think Jesus may just be tricking the people.
original.longDescription:
In the first century, a group of children meet together to talk about what they've seen and heard about Jesus. Some believe Jesus is the Son of God. But others think Jesus may just be tricking the people.

The children follow Jesus around, witness His miracles, and listen to Him teach. Jesus raises a girl from the dead, calls imperfect people like tax collectors to follow Him, teaches everyone to be kind and gracious to each other, and lets a woman wash His feet with tears. He teaches in parables no one really understands, calms a raging storm, gives sight to the blind, and helps those who no one sees as worth helping. He shows the children an amazing, powerful, and kind way to live. Benjamin and Sarah talk to the children watching their story about Jesus and what it means to believe who He is and accept Him as their Savior.

original.title: उद्धारकर्ता
original.shortDescription: The Savior provides an introduction to Jesus through the Gospel of Luke, during the time when Rome ruled much of the world. This was a time of political strife and social unrest, and it was into this environment that Jesus was born. Much is recorded in the Gospels but little is known about his quiet time of growing up in Nazareth. Later he teaches in parables no one really understands, gives sight to the blind, and helps those who no one sees as worth helping. The Savior is a fresh portrayal of the life of Jesus with dialogue taken directly from the Gospel of Luke. It follows Jesus from his upbringing to his death and resurrection.

sections.title: Old Testament Overview
sections.description: Animated overviews of every book of the Old Testament, showing each book's literary design and how it contributes to the unified biblical story.

items.title: TaNaK / Old Testament Overview
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: తనాక్ / పాత నిబంధన  TaNaK / OT Overview
items.description: Did you know that the arrangement of the Old Testament in Protestant Christian Bibles is not original? Along with all ancient Jewish people, Jesus encountered the Scriptures as a three-part collection of scrolls known as the TaNaK, an acronym for the three large subcollections of the Hebrew Bible: Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets), and Ketuvim (Writings).

items.title: Genesis 1-11
items.description: In chapters 1-11, the book of Genesis recounts God's good world and humanity's repeated rebellion. How will God restore blessing to the world? We find the answer in the family of Abraham.

items.title: Genesis 12-50
items.description: Through Abraham's family, God promises to bless all nations. Genesis follows four generations of human failure set against God's continued faithfulness. As Joseph says, 'You planned this for evil, but God planned it for good' (Gen. 50:20). The book ends with the promise of a future king who will restore blessing to the nations.

items.title: Exodus 1-18
items.description: How does God respond when his people cry out to him? The first part of the book of Exodus recounts a powerful confrontation between God and the unjust Pharaoh. This section is a fast-paced narrative that leads to divine justice, rescue, and deliverance.

items.title: Exodus 19-40
items.description: The first part of Exodus shows God freeing Israel from Egypt. Then, at Mount Sinai, Moses receives God's law, but Israel breaks the covenant. Moses pleads with God, who renews his promises. After the tabernacle is built, God's glory fills it, but Moses can't enter due to his own rebellion.

items.title: Leviticus
items.description: God made a covenant with Israel and brought his own presence to dwell with them. However, Israel cannot enter his presence because of their corruption. In response, God introduces a set of sacrifices, the priesthood, and purity laws in the book of Leviticus.

items.title: Numbers
items.description: The book of Numbers tells the story of Israel's repeated rebellion in the wilderness and how it is met by God's justice and mercy. God responds with short-term severity and long-term generosity that speaks to his covenant faithfulness.

items.title: Deuteronomy
items.description: In the book of Deuteronomy, Moses gives Israel final words of warning and blessing. He covers the story so far, a collection of laws, and a charge for Israel to listen and obey rather than rebel. Moses knows the people well enough to know they will eventually choose rebellion, yet Moses looked forward to their promised hope.

items.title: Joshua
items.description: The book of Joshua shows us God's covenant faithfulness to bring the Israelites into the land he promised Abraham. This book points to the importance of covenant obedience before, during, and after God fulfills his promises.

items.title: Judges
items.description: After the death of Joshua, the people of Israel begin a downward spiral. The book of Judges highlights six judges and their increasing corruption during this time. The central verse that summarizes this says, 'In those days Israel had no king, and everyone did what was right in their own eyes.'

items.title: Ruth
items.description: The book of Ruth follows Naomi, her Moabite daughter-in-law, Ruth, and the farmer Boaz during the time of the judges. Though God is rarely mentioned directly, he works through their everyday faithfulness. Their story of tragedy turned to joy becomes part of the line of King David and ultimately the Messiah.

items.title: 1 Samuel
items.description: The book of 1 Samuel focuses on three characters: Samuel, Saul, and David. A poem near the start of the book reveals the book's key themes: God's opposition to the proud, exultation of the humble, faithfulness in spite of evil, and the promise of a messianic king.

items.title: 2 Samuel
items.description: The book of 2 Samuel continues to show us the virtue of humility, the destructiveness of pride, and the faithfulness of God's promise. We see David succeed and fail, and we see God's promise for a future king at the beginning and end of the story.

items.title: Ezra-Nehemiah
items.description: This book recounts the people's return from exile and the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem. Nehemiah rebuilds the walls, and Ezra, a descendant of Aaron, arrives in Jerusalem later and instills God's laws to the post-exile generation.

items.title: Esther
items.description: Though God is never mentioned in the book of Esther, we can see clearly that he is at work behind the scenes, ensuring that Haman's plot to destroy the Jewish people is thwarted. Reading Esther reminds us that even when it seems like God is absent, he is still at work in our lives and will not abandon his promises.

items.title: Job
items.description: Job, his wife, and his friends continually speculate on why an upright man like Job might experience so much suffering. God reminds Job that the world has order and beauty but it is also wild and dangerous. While we do not always know why we suffer, we can bring our pain and grief to God and trust his wisdom.

items.title: Psalms
items.description: The book of Psalms is a carefully designed collection of poetry that communicates key ideas about God's character. It's a book made for a lifetime of careful contemplation, where we can learn about the importance of prayer and the acknowledgment of pain, as well as the power of praise and fulfillment of prophecy.

items.title: Proverbs
items.description: Linked to Solomon and other wise men, the book of Proverbs includes hundreds of short, clever sayings designed to teach us how to live and act wisely. Each saying touches on a common area of life and shows us what it looks like to live well in God's good world.

items.title: Ecclesiastes
items.description: The book of Ecclesiastes is the author's response to Proverbs. From their perspective, life isn't so simple as fearing God and choosing wisdom. Life is unpredictable, and our existence is a blip of time. In their words, 'it's all hevel,' meaning temporary or fleeting. So is there any point at all? Yes, but it may surprise you.

items.title: Song of Songs
items.description: Song of Songs, also known as the Song of Solomon, is not technically a book. It's a love song between two lovers—and it works on two levels. Song of Songs is celebrating human's desire for intimacy and pointing to humanity's ultimate purpose: to be united with God and his wisdom.

items.title: Isaiah 1-39
items.description: The book of Isaiah is filled with sobering accounts of Israel's sin and rebellion and warnings of their coming judgement. But along with warnings, Isaiah also offers a message of hope—a suffering servant, a Messiah, will come to establish God's Kingdom on Earth and create a new Jerusalem.

items.title: Isaiah 40-66
items.description: Isaiah calls for Israel and the surrounding rebellious nations to repent and turn to God, warning of the judgment that will come if they do not. But Isaiah's message is not without hope. He continually points to a coming servant, Immanuel, who will establish a new Israel and bring God's Kingdom to Earth. Jesus reads from the scroll of Isaiah and declares that the book's messianic promises were being fulfilled in him.

items.title: Jeremiah
items.description: The prophet Jeremiah announced that God would judge Israel's sins with exile to Babylon. And then he lived through the horror of his predictions. The book of Jeremiah shows a graphic but important picture of how disobedience leads to destruction.

items.title: Lamentations
items.description: Lamentations is a collection of poems detailing Israel's grief after Jerusalem's destruction, which was caused by their rebellion against God. In these laments, the people confess sins and seek restoration, showing us that expressing our distress to God is an appropriate response to suffering.

items.title: Ezekiel 1-33
items.description: Ezekiel is a prophet living in exile in Babylon. Ezekiel boldly speaks God's message of Israel's rebellion and makes clear that this exile is punishment for their covenant unfaithfulness. God's presence being revealed to Ezekiel demonstrates that holiness has nothing to do with geographical location—it's about the condition of the heart. God is moved by the faithfulness of men like Ezekiel, who became his priest not because of status but because of his faith in dark circumstances. His example is a model for believers everywhere.

items.title: Ezekiel 34-48
items.description: Ezekiel is a prophet living in exile in Babylon. God's presence being revealed to Ezekiel demonstrates that holiness has nothing to do with geographical location—it's about the condition of the heart. God is moved by the faithfulness of men like Ezekiel, who became his priest not because of status but because of his faith in dark circumstances.

items.title: Daniel
items.description: The book of Daniel is apocalyptic literature that includes several strange visions that point to the coming Son of Man, the messianic King who will deliver Israel and the nations. Daniel is also about hope and faith in the midst of exile, as Daniel remains faithful to Yahweh and hopeful for the restoration of Israel.

items.title: Hosea
items.description: In the book of Hosea, God sends Hosea to Israel during the reign of King Jeroboam II to communicate God's despair over their perpetual idol worship and dependence on outside nations. Though the people have failed to be faithful covenant partners to God, his commitment to them remains.

items.title: Joel
items.description: The prophet Joel speaks about the Day of the Lord, a day when evil empires will be brought low and God's people will be finally delivered from corrupt human systems. Though Israel's sin is never specifically mentioned in the book, Joel is clear that God will not allow evil to continue wreaking havoc on his good world.

items.title: Amos
items.description: God calls a Judean shepherd named Amos to confront the wrongdoing of the people of Israel, offering them one more chance before they face God's judgement. God is grieved by the evils he sees the people of Israel doing, but he mercifully offers them another chance to change their ways.

items.title: Obadiah
items.description: The book of Obadiah may be small, but it packs a powerful punch against the arrogance of Edom and other ungodly nations. Through Obadiah, God declares judgment over Edom and prophesies that they will be erased from history. Babylon overtook Edom 100 years later, and they never recovered.

items.title: Jonah
items.description: The book of Jonah poses fascinating questions for us to ponder. Do we truly forgive and love our enemies? And do we run from God when faced with our failures? By examining ourselves through Jonah's story, we can learn to trust God in his decisions and give all our concerns to him, knowing that he desires to save every individual and reunite with them forever.

items.title: Micah
items.description: The prophet Micah describes God's coming judgment on Israel because it has exploited the poor and twisted the laws of the Torah. But Micah's prophecies are not without hope. The God of Israel is also faithful and full of mercy. God promises to preserve a faithful remnant, from which he will create a new Jerusalem on the other side of sin and exile.

items.title: Nahum
items.description: The book of Nahum is a collection of poems announcing the downfall of some of Israel's worst oppressors. Referencing Daniel, Exodus, and Isaiah, Nahum shows us that the destruction of Nineveh and Assyria are examples of how God works in history in every age.

items.title: Habakkuk
items.description: Throughout the book of Habakkuk, we see that Babylon is an example of any nation that exalts itself above God and practices injustice, violence, and idolatry. In the end, God reminds Habakkuk and every generation that God will deal with evil. We can continue to love and trust his timing and plan as we remain faithful to him.

items.title: Zephaniah
items.description: The book of Zephaniah contains intense images of God's justice and hope. Zephaniah warns Israel and the surrounding nations that God will judge the nations with a burning fire as he purifies them from sin, evil, and violence. But this purification will open up a new future where all of humanity can flourish.

items.title: Haggai
items.description: Haggai challenges the returning exiles to remember their covenant, remain faithful to God, and build the temple before constructing their own homes. They can be encouraged by God's promise to build a new Jerusalem, defeat evil, and live in their midst. Future prophetic books contain more details about when these promises will be fulfilled.

items.title: Zechariah
items.description: The book of Zechariah contains a series of dream visions filled with bizarre images. And even though the book doesn't follow a neat, orderly pattern, it shows God's hand guiding history toward his purposes. We can look above the chaos and hope for the coming of God's Kingdom, which will motivate faithfulness in the present.

items.title: Malachi
items.description: The book of Malachi is a stark indictment of Israel's rebellion, but it offers a surprising message of hope too. Even after years of rebellion and exile, God has not abandoned Israel. God promises to defeat evil and purify a faithful remnant, establishing a new Jerusalem and bringing peace, healing, and justice forever.

items.title: 1 & 2 Chronicles
items.description: As the last book in the Hebrew Bible, Chronicles invites its readers to explore the stories of each section, revealing interesting details about David, Solomon, God's temple, and the kings of Judah. The book ultimately leaves the reader waiting for the promised Messiah, who will restore Israel to their covenant partnership with God.

sections.title: New Testament Overview
sections.description: Animated overviews of every book of the New Testament, showing each book's literary design and how it contributes to the unified biblical story.

items.title: Matthew 1-13
items.description: Matthew begins with a genealogy that shows Jesus as a descendant from the line of David, a king and a fulfillment of God's covenant promises to David and all of Israel.

items.title: Matthew 14-28
items.description: Matthew's gospel opens with Jesus' genealogy, showing him as David's descendant and fulfillment of God's promises to Israel.

items.title: Mark
items.description: The Gospel of Mark gives a thorough account of Jesus' life and ministry without making a clear statement about Jesus' identity, and this is intentional.

items.title: Luke 1-9
items.description: Luke documents how Jesus expands God's Kingdom and covenant by creating a new Israel that includes the poor, outcasts, and others.

items.title: Luke 10-24
items.description: Luke documents how Jesus expands God's Kingdom and covenant by creating a new Israel that includes the poor and outcasts.

items.title: John 1-12
items.description: John's Gospel emphasizes Jesus' identity as the Messiah and Son of God. Because of this divine identity, Jesus is able to give eternal life to everyone who believes in him.

items.title: John 13-21
items.description: John's Gospel emphasizes Jesus' identity as the Messiah and Son of God. Because of this divine identity, Jesus is able to give eternal life to everyone who believes in him.

items.title: Acts 1-12
items.description: Jesus' followers received the Holy Spirit on Pentecost and became filled and equipped to spread the good news that would restore God's kingdom over the world.

items.title: Acts 13-28
items.description: Jesus' followers received the Holy Spirit at Pentecost and were equipped to spread the good news that would restore God's Kingdom on Earth.

items.title: Romans 1-4
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: రోమీయులకు రాసిన పత్రిక 1 వ భాగము Overview: Romans 1-4
items.description: The people of Israel tried to obey God and follow the law, but they didn't succeed. Only faith in Jesus' death and resurrection can justify humanity.

items.title: Romans 5-16
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: రోమీయులకు రాసిన పత్రిక 2 వ భాగము Overview: Romans 5-16
items.description: Paul's letter shows how the resurrection gives reasons for unity, motivation for sexual purity, and ability to love others.

items.title: 1 Corinthians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: కొరింథీయులకు రాసిన  1 పత్రిక Overview: 1 Corinthians
items.description: Paul's first letter to the Corinthians is a wake-up call: the resurrection gives us a reason for unity, motivation to maintain sexual purity.

items.title: 2 Corinthians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: కొరింథీయులకు రాసిన 2వ పత్రిక Overview: 2 Corinthians
items.description: In 2 Corinthians, Paul challenges followers of Jesus to see life through the paradox of the cross.

items.title: Galatians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: గలతీయులకు రాసిన పత్రిక Overview: Galatians
items.description: In the book of Galatians, followers of Jesus learn that they are justified by the Gospel of Jesus, not the laws of Torah.

items.title: Ephesians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: ఎఫెసీయులకు రాసిన పత్రిక Overview: Ephesians
items.description: In the book of Ephesians, we learn how the Gospel creates a new multi-ethnic, covenant family of God.

items.title: Philippians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: ఫిలిప్పీయులకు రాసిన పత్రిక  Overview: Philippians
items.description: The book of Philippians shows how living as a Christian means seeing your story as a living expression of Jesus' story.

items.title: Colossians
items.description: The book of Colossians addresses problems the church at Colossae faced, challenging followers of Jesus to examine their lives.

items.title: 1 Thessalonians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: థెస్సలోనీకయులకు రాసిన 1 ఉత్తరం Overview: 1 Thessalonians
items.description: In 1 Thessalonians, Paul celebrates the Church's holiness, love, and future hope as they remain faithful to Jesus.

items.title: 2 Thessalonians
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: థెస్సలోనికయులకు రాసిన 2 పత్రిక  Overview: 2 Thessalonians
items.description: In his second letter to the Thessalonians, Paul encourages the church to remain faithful, hopeful, confident, and fearless.

items.title: 1 Timothy
items.description: In this letter, Paul instructs Timothy on how to address corrupt leaders who are sharing false teachings in the church of Ephesus.

items.title: 2 Timothy
items.description: 2 Timothy is Paul's last letter. It was written to encourage Timothy, challenging him to fully accept his calling.

items.title: Titus
items.title_vernacular: సారాంశం: తీతుకు రాసిన పత్రిక  Overview: Titus
items.description: In the book of Titus, Paul reminds Cretan believers that, despite their sinful culture, they can be transformed into a new humanity.

items.title: Philemon
items.description: In this book, Paul asks Philemon to forgive his runaway slave, Onesimus. This is a revolutionary act.

items.title: Hebrews
items.description: The book of Hebrews challenges believers to remain faithful to Jesus despite hardships and persecution.

items.title: James
items.description: The book of James is filled with short wisdom speeches that are full of metaphors and easily memorized one-liners.

items.title: 1 Peter
items.description: This letter was written as an encouragement to Gentile Christians facing persecution.

items.title: 2 Peter
items.description: In this letter, Peter issues two warnings against corrupt teachers, who are objecting to the reality of Jesus' resurrection.

items.title: 1-3 John
items.description: The books of 1, 2, and 3 John address a changing tide in the early Church—deceivers and teachers who no longer acknowledge Jesus.

items.title: Jude
items.description: The book of Jude references the Hebrew Bible and Jewish literature to illustrate God's judgment on rebellion.

items.title: Revelation 1-11
items.description: The book of Revelation is not a secret code for deciphering the timeline of Jesus' return. It's a work of apocalyptic literature.

items.title: Revelation 12-22
items.description: The book of Revelation is not a secret code for deciphering the timeline of Jesus' return. It's a work of apocalyptic literature.

sections.title: Biblical Themes
sections.description: Animated videos tracing key biblical themes through the entire story of the Bible, from Genesis to Revelation.

items.title: God
items.description: The God portrayed in the Bible isn't easy to understand, but what if we could better understand what it is that we can't understand? This video explores God's complex identity in the biblical narrative and Jesus's role as both unified with and distinct from the Father.

items.title: Justice
items.description: Justice is a felt need in our world today and a controversial topic. But what is justice exactly, and who gets to define it? In this video, we'll explore the biblical theme of justice and discover how it's deeply rooted in the storyline of the Bible that leads to Jesus.

items.title: The Messiah
items.description: Explore the mysterious promise on page three of the Bible, that a promised deliverer would one day come to confront evil and rescue humanity. We trace this theme through the family of Abraham, the messianic lineage of David, and ultimately to Jesus who defeated evil by letting it defeat him.

items.title: Holy Spirit
items.description: In this video, we explore the original meaning of the biblical concept of spirit (ruakh) and what it means that God's Spirit is personally present in all of creation. Ultimately, the Spirit was revealed through Jesus and sent out into the lives of his followers to bring about the new creation.

items.title: Image of God
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ అంశాలు: దేవుని స్వరూపం Image of God
items.description: What does it mean for humans to be made in God's image? In the opening pages of Genesis, we see God create humanity as his co-rulers of creation, but things quickly go wrong when humans rebel and forfeit their role. Jesus comes to set right humanity's rebellion, opening up a new way of being human through his life, death, and resurrection.

items.title: Tree of Life
items.title_vernacular: బైబిలు అంశాలు: జీవవ్రుక్షం Tree of Life
items.description: In the opening pages of the Bible, God gives humanity a gift that they quickly forfeit: eternal life that comes by eating from the tree of life. Sacred trees are a powerful symbol woven throughout Scripture, culminating in the dramatic climax of Jesus' death. His crucifixion on a cross transforms a tree of death into a new tree of life for all humanity.

items.title: Water of Life
items.title_vernacular: బైబిలు అంశాలు:  జీవ జలం Water of Life
items.description: In the beginning of the Bible, God transforms a desolate wilderness into a garden through a stream that waters the ground and brings life wherever it goes. Water imagery continues to develop throughout the biblical story where we see wells, cisterns, rain, and rivers all become images of God's creative power.

items.title: Heaven and Earth
items.description: What does the Bible really teach about Heaven, and what is Heaven's relationship to Earth? In this video, we explore the surprising biblical viewpoint that Heaven and Earth were meant to overlap and how Jesus is on a mission to bring them together once and for all.

items.title: Temple
items.description: The biblical authors describe Israel's temple as the place where God's space and human space overlap. In fact, the whole biblical drama can be told as a story about God's temple: God creates a cosmic temple and, in Jesus, takes up residence in his temple-world. By the end of the biblical story, all of creation has become God's sacred temple.

items.title: Sabbath
items.description: The Bible opens with God creating an ordered world from chaos in six days before resting on the seventh day. This pattern of seven that ends with divine-human rest echoes throughout Scripture. Jesus embraces this theme in his mission to establish God's Kingdom on Earth, where humanity and God will finally rest together.

items.title: Holiness
items.description: God's holiness presents a paradox to human beings. God is the unique and set-apart Creator of all reality and the author of all goodness. However, that goodness can become dangerous to humans who are morally corrupt. Ultimately, this paradox is resolved by Jesus, who embodies God's holiness that came to heal his creation.

items.title: Sacrifice and Atonement
items.description: God is on a mission to remove evil from his good world, along with all of its corrosive effects. However, he wants to do it in a way that doesn't involve removing humans. In this video, we trace the theme of God's 'covering' over human evil through animal sacrifices that ultimately point to Jesus and his death and resurrection.

items.title: Day of the Lord
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ అంశాలు: ప్రభువు దినం Day of the Lord
items.description: Does God still care about the destruction humans have caused in his good world? The story of the Bible shows us how God confronts human evil, as well as the deeper spiritual evil that is at work on Earth. Ultimately, we see how Jesus responds to the problem of evil by allowing his death on the cross.

items.title: The Law
items.description: What is the importance of the ancient laws in the Hebrew Bible? Are they even relevant for Jesus followers? Explore how much the laws can teach us about God's character and the significance of Jesus' ministry on Earth.

items.title: Son of Man
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ అంశాలు: మనుష్య కుమారుడు Son of Man
items.description: If you thought Christ was Jesus' last name or the title he gave himself, think again! The title Jesus most often used for himself is the Son of Man. But what does that mean? In this video, we'll explore the meaning of this fascinating phrase and see how it invites us into the larger biblical story.

items.title: Gospel of the Kingdom
items.description: Gospel is a word that means 'good news,' but it's more than that. It's a royal announcement, and its use in the New Testament points to the radical announcement of God's Kingdom coming to Earth through Jesus. The Gospel fulfills the promises of the Hebrew Bible, as we see Jesus bring God's reign and rule in a way no one expected.

items.title: Covenant
items.description: Despite human rebellion, God continues to make covenant promises to restore humanity to the role they were created for: to be partners with God in ruling creation. Though humans repeatedly fail, Jesus fulfills humanity's side of the partnership, making right the relationship between God and humankind.

items.title: Exile
items.description: Exile is one of the core, yet often overlooked, themes underlying the entire biblical storyline. In this video, we'll see how Israel's exile to Babylon is a picture of all humanity's exile from Eden. We are all exiles longing for home, and Jesus is the one to open the way back to our true home and the fullness of relationship with God.

items.title: Generosity
items.description: In the story of the Bible, God is depicted as a generous host who provides for the needs of his guests. However, humans live from a mindset of scarcity and hoard God's many gifts. In this video, we explore God's plan for overcoming our selfishness by giving the ultimate gift of himself in the person of Jesus.

items.title: Blessing and Curse
items.description: 'Blessing' is a religious-sounding word that we use a lot. We say, 'Bless you!' after a sneeze, or that we're 'so blessed' when life is good. But what does blessing mean in the Bible? In this video, we trace the theme of blessing and curse in the Bible to see how Jesus defeats the curse and restores the blessing of life to creation.

items.title: Chaos Dragon
items.description: In the ancient world, the sea dragon was a common symbol that represented death and chaos. But the story of the Bible begins with God demonstrating his power over all creatures. While both spiritual and human forces threaten to pull creation into disorder, Jesus defeats the darkness by trusting God to bring life out of death.

items.title: The City
items.description: Why does the Bible open with a garden as the ideal space but close with a heavenly city? Explore the surprising theme of the city in the Bible.

items.title: Firstborn
items.description: In the New Testament, Jesus is called the 'firstborn,' a title of authority. While firstborns traditionally received inheritance and power in the ancient world, Jesus redefines this power. In his Kingdom, the last are first, and true authority comes through loving others, even our enemies.

items.title: Anointing
items.description: Explore an ancient practice that marks people and places as bridges between Heaven and Earth.

items.title: Eternal Life
items.description: Why does God sometimes lead his people into harsh and isolated places? Trace the theme of the wilderness through the story of the Bible and discover how trusting God in the wilderness prepares us for life in the garden.

sections.title: How to Read the Bible
sections.description: A series exploring the art of reading the Bible, covering its literary styles, narrative techniques, and design patterns.

items.title: What is the Bible?
items.description: Unpack the history and origins of this extraordinary collection of writings to look closer at what you'll find in your Bible today.

items.title: The Story of the Bible
items.description: The Bible is a collection of writings that tells one unified story about God's plan to partner with humanity to rule a united Heaven and Earth.

items.title: Literary Styles in the Bible
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ సాహితీ శైలి Literary Styles in the Bible
items.description: Reading the Bible wisely requires that we learn about the ancient literary styles used by the biblical authors. But why did these writers express their ideas and claims through a variety of different types of literature? What was the purpose, and how can we understand them better?

items.title: Ancient Jewish Meditation Literature
items.description: The Bible is a multi-layered work, offering levels of insight as you re-read and meditate on the Bible. Explore the unique style of the Bible, which is meant to draw its readers into a lifelong journey of reading and meditation.

items.title: The Torah
items.description: The Torah refers to the first five books of the Bible: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy. These books lay the foundation for the entire biblical story, introducing God's relationship with humanity, the covenant with Israel, and the laws given at Mount Sinai.

items.title: The Prophets
items.description: The books of the Old Testament prophets are packed with dense poetry and wild imagery. If you've tried to read them, odds are you were both intrigued and confused. In this video, we'll learn how these prophetic books contribute to the storyline of the Bible and why it's worth learning how to read them more attentively.

items.title: Plot in Biblical Narrative
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ కథనంలో కథా వస్తువు Plot In Biblical Narrative
items.description: An important part of reading biblical narratives is learning how to understand the nature of how stories are arranged into a pattern of conflict and resolution. When we pick out verses and read them apart from the context of their overall plot, we can fail to interpret the intended meaning of the story.

items.title: Character in Biblical Narrative
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ కథనంలో పాత్రలు Character in Biblical Narrative
items.description: Most of us think of characters in the Bible as either sinners or saints, good or bad. At least that's how Bible stories are presented to children. In this video, we'll explore the ways biblical authors present characters as more complex and morally compromised than we usually imagine.

items.title: Setting in Biblical Narrative
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ కథనంలో సన్నివేశం Setting in Biblical Narrative
items.description: Every story takes place somewhere, and locations often have a special meaning evoked by past events in the same location. We call these locations settings, and biblical authors use settings to meet the reader's expectations—and mess with them. When we pay attention to locations and time in biblical stories, we can unlock deeper layers of meaning.

items.title: Design Patterns in Biblical Narrative
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ కథనంలో రూపకల్పన నమూనాలు Design Patterns in Biblical Narrative
items.description: Design patterns are one of the key ways the biblical authors have unified the storyline of the Bible. Individual stories across the Old and New Testaments have been coordinated through repeated words and parallel themes. These patterns highlight core themes of the biblical story and show how it all leads to Jesus.

items.title: Poetry
items.description: Did you know that a third of the Bible is ancient Israelite poetry? Poetry is a rich and artistic form of human communication, but it's also some of the most difficult to read. In this video, we'll explore the unique characteristics of biblical poetry and discover its beauty and power.

items.title: Metaphor in Biblical Poetry
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ కవిత్వంలో ఉపమాలంకారం Metaphor in Biblical Poetry
items.description: Understanding how metaphors are used in the Bible is an essential tool for reading biblical poetry. Anytime someone describes one thing to give meaning to something else, they are using metaphorical thinking. Metaphors are everywhere in the Bible and in our everyday speech. In this video, we'll explore this crucial aspect of biblical language.

items.title: The Art of Biblical Poetry
items.title_vernacular: బైబిల్ పద్య కవిత్వం The Art of Biblical Poetry
items.description: Did you know that a third of the Bible is ancient Israelite poetry? Poetry is a rich and artistic form of human communication, but it's also some of the most difficult to read. In this video, we'll explore the unique characteristics of biblical poetry and discover its beauty and power.

items.title: The Book of Psalms
items.title_vernacular: కీర్తనలు గ్రంథం The Book of Psalms
items.description: The book of Psalms is the largest collection of poetry in the Bible. In this video, we'll explore the design, shape, and main themes of this marvelous book, which was crafted to be read from beginning to end. The Psalms are an invitation to a literary temple, where you can meet with God and hear the entire biblical storyline retold in poetic form.

items.title: Apocalyptic Literature
items.description: The Bible is filled with dreams and visions about human history coming to a climax, and they're usually packed with intense imagery and strange symbols. In this video, we'll explore the meaning of the word "apocalypse" in the Bible and learn some basic steps for reading this literature with more wisdom and insight.

items.title: Parables of Jesus
items.title_vernacular: బైబిలును ఎలా చదవాలి: యేసు ఉపమానాలు The Parables of Jesus
items.description: Jesus of Nazareth was a master storyteller, and many of his most well-known teachings were told as parables. But why did Jesus use parables to communicate his message so often? Why didn't he speak in plain language so that everyone could understand him? The answer may be surprising.

items.title: The Gospels
items.description: The New Testament contains four ancient biographies of Jesus of Nazareth, and altogether they are called "the Gospel." Each one tells the story as an announcement of good news that the crucified and risen Jesus is the true ruler of the nations. In this video, we explore why these accounts were written and how you can read them with greater insight.

items.title: New Testament Letters
items.title_vernacular: కొత్త నిబంధన పత్రికల సాహిత్యం New Testament Letters
items.description: In the New Testament, there are 21 letters written by early Christian leaders to communities of Jesus' followers in the ancient Roman world. These letters are rich with theology and guidance for what it means to be a community of Jesus followers. But it can be easy to miss the meaning of these letters when we don't consider their context. In this video, we break down the historical context of the New Testament letters.

sections.title: Spiritual Beings
sections.description: Videos exploring the spiritual beings described in the Bible, from angels and cherubim to the divine council.

items.title: Intro to Spiritual Beings
items.description: In the opening pages of the Bible, God creates two overlapping realms, the heavens and the earth. The video introduces viewers to spiritual characters heavily involved in the earthly drama alongside human participants.

items.title: Elohim
items.description: This segment examines how 'elohim,' the biblical word for God, functions as a title rather than a name and can reference both the creator and other spiritual beings, clarifying what 'God is one' means.

items.title: Divine Council
items.title_vernacular: దైవిక సలహా మండలి The Divine Council
items.description: What is the divine council? This biblical phrase is used to describe God's heavenly 'staff team.' The video explains how these spiritual powers were created for authority alongside humans, detailing their rebellion and Jesus's role in resolution.

items.title: Angels and Cherubim
items.description: Correcting popular misconceptions, this episode reveals that biblical angels lack wings and cherubim aren't depicted as cute infants, exploring their actual roles within scripture's narrative.

items.title: The Angel of the Lord
items.title_vernacular: యెహోవా దూత Angel of the Lord
items.description: This video investigates the paradoxical 'Angel of the Lord' figure in Hebrew Scripture, depicted simultaneously as God and God's messenger, preparing viewers for New Testament claims about Jesus.

items.title: Satan and Demons
items.description: The Bible describes a spiritual world full of creatures who are in rebellion against their Creator. The video traces these spiritual themes from Genesis, showing how darkness challenges divine authority.

items.title: The New Humanity
items.description: Beginning with humans appointed to rule on God's behalf, this concluding episode follows scripture's search for faithful partners who will fulfill the role humanity abandoned through rebellion.

sections.title: Word Studies
sections.description: Animated word studies exploring the original Hebrew and Greek words behind key biblical concepts.

items.title: Shalom
items.description: Shalom is a Hebrew word that means much more than 'peace.' It refers to completeness, wholeness, and the way things ought to be. The biblical authors use shalom to describe God's intention for the world—a place where everything and everyone flourishes together in harmony.

items.title: Agape
items.description: Agape is a Greek word used in the New Testament to describe God's generous, self-giving love for humanity. It refers to a love that is unconditional and costly—the kind of love displayed in Jesus' sacrificial life, death, and resurrection.

items.title: Shema
items.description: The Shema, from the Hebrew word meaning 'listen' or 'hear,' is the central prayer and confession of faith in ancient Israel. Found in Deuteronomy 6:4-5, it calls God's people to love the Lord with all their heart, soul, and strength—an invitation to wholehearted devotion.

items.title: Meod
items.description: The list of God's character traits found in Exodus 34:6-7 is the most repeated and re-quoted text in the Bible. But what does it mean when God describes himself as compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, and overflowing with loyal love and faithfulness? Understanding the significance of these Hebrew words will bring God's character into clearer focus.

items.title: వాక్యము శరీరధారి ఆయెను
items.description: దేవునియొద్ద ఉండి దేవుడైయున్న నిత్యమైన వాక్యము యేసులో శరీరధారి ఆయెనని ఈ సువార్త ఆరంభమవుతుంది. బాప్తిస్మమిచ్చు యోహాను ఆయనను గూర్చి సాక్ష్యమిచ్చును, అంద్రెయ మెస్సీయ అని పిలిచిన ఆయనను మొదటి శిష్యులు వెంబడించుదురు.

items.title: కానాలో వివాహము
items.description: కానాలో జరిగిన ఒక వివాహములో యేసు నీళ్లను ద్రాక్షారసముగా మార్చును; ఇదే ఆయన సూచక క్రియలలో మొదటిది. తరువాత ఆయన యెరూషలేములోని దేవాలయములోనుండి వర్తకులను, రూకలు మార్చువారిని వెళ్లగొట్టును.

items.title: మీరు క్రొత్తగా జన్మింపవలెను
items.description: నీకొదేము రాత్రివేళ యేసునొద్దకు వచ్చి, క్రొత్తగా జన్మింపనివాడెవడును దేవుని రాజ్యమును చూడలేడని వినును. దేవుడు లోకమును ఎంతో ప్రేమించి తన అద్వితీయ కుమారుని అనుగ్రహించెను.

items.title: బావియొద్ద సమరయ స్త్రీ
items.description: యాకోబు బావియొద్ద యేసు ఒక సమరయ స్త్రీకి జీవజలము ఇచ్చుటకు ఇష్టపడును, అనేకమంది సమరయులు ఆయనయందు విశ్వాసముంచుదురు. గలిలయకు తిరిగివచ్చి, ఆయన ఒక రాజోద్యోగి యొక్క మరణావస్థలోనున్న కుమారుని ఒక మాటతో స్వస్థపరచును.

items.title: బేతెస్ద కోనేటియొద్ద స్వస్థత
items.description: ముప్పది యెనిమిది సంవత్సరములనుండి రోగియైయున్న ఒక మనుష్యుని యేసు విశ్రాంతిదినమున స్వస్థపరచును. పెద్దలు అభ్యంతరపెట్టినప్పుడు, కుమారుడు జీవమిచ్చునని, తన తండ్రి క్రియలను చేయుచున్నాడని యేసు ప్రకటించును.

items.title: జీవాహారము
items.description: ఐదు రొట్టెలతోను రెండు చేపలతోను యేసు ఐదువేలమందికి భోజనము పెట్టి, తరువాత సముద్రముమీద నడచి తన శిష్యులయొద్దకు వచ్చును. తానే జీవాహారమని ప్రకటించగా అనేకులు ఆయనను విడిచిపోవుట ఆయన చూచును, అయితే నిత్యజీవపు మాటలు ఆయనయొద్దనే యున్నవని పేతురు ఒప్పుకొనును.

items.title: పర్ణశాలల పండుగలో
items.description: యేసు రహస్యముగా యెరూషలేమునకు వెళ్లి, తరువాత దేవాలయ ప్రాంగణములలో బహిరంగముగా బోధించును. పండుగ చివరి దినమున దప్పికగొనినవారిని తనయొద్దకు వచ్చి త్రాగుడని ఆహ్వానించును, ఆయన ఎవరనే విషయమై జనసమూహము విభజింపబడును.

items.title: లోకమునకు వెలుగు
items.description: వ్యభిచారములో పట్టుబడిన స్త్రీని యేసు శిక్షించుటకు నిరాకరించి, పాపజీవితమును విడిచిపెట్టుమని ఆమెతో చెప్పును. తానే లోకమునకు వెలుగునని ప్రకటించి, 'అబ్రాహాము పుట్టకమునుపే నేను ఉన్నాను' అని తనమీద నేరము మోపువారితో చెప్పును.

items.title: పుట్టుగ్రుడ్డివాడు
items.description: పుట్టుగ్రుడ్డియైన ఒక మనుష్యుని కన్నులకు యేసు పూయగా, అతడు సిలోయము కోనేటిలో కడుగుకొని చూపు పొందును. పరిసయ్యులు అతని విచారించి వెలివేయుదురు, ఆ మనుష్యుడు యేసును మనుష్యకుమారునిగా ఆరాధించును.

items.title: మంచి కాపరి
items.title_vernacular: ఐదు వేల మందికి భోజనం మరియు నీళ్ల మీద నడవడం
items.description: గొఱ్ఱెలకొరకు తన ప్రాణము పెట్టు మంచి కాపరి యేసే, ఆయన గొఱ్ఱెలు ఆయన స్వరము ఎరుగును. ప్రతిష్ఠాపండుగలో 'నేనును తండ్రియు ఏకమై యున్నాము' అని ఆయన ప్రకటించగా, పెద్దలు ఆయనను పట్టుకొనుటకు ప్రయత్నించుదురు.

items.title: లాజరును లేపుట
items.description: తన స్నేహితుడైన లాజరు సమాధియొద్ద యేసు కన్నీరు విడిచి, నాలుగు దినముల తరువాత అతని సమాధిలోనుండి పిలుచును. ఈ సూచక క్రియవలన అనేకులు విశ్వసించుదురు, యేసు చావవలెనని మహాసభ నిర్ణయించును.

items.title: గడియ వచ్చియున్నది
items.description: బేతనియలో మరియ యేసు పాదములకు అత్తరు పూయును, ఆయన 'హోసన్నా' అను కేకల మధ్య యెరూషలేములో ప్రవేశించును. నేలలో పడి చచ్చు గోధుమగింజవలె, మనుష్యకుమారుడు మహిమపరచబడు గడియ వచ్చియున్నదని యేసు ప్రకటించును.

items.title: శిష్యుల పాదములు కడుగుట
items.description: అంతిమ భోజనమునందు యేసు తన శిష్యుల పాదములు కడిగి, తాను చేసినట్టు వారును చేయవలెనని చెప్పును. యూదా తనను అప్పగించుటను, పేతురు తనను ఎరుగననుటను ముందుగా తెలియజేసి, ఒకనినొకడు ప్రేమించుడని క్రొత్త ఆజ్ఞ ఇచ్చును.

items.title: మార్గము, సత్యము, జీవము
items.description: యేసు తన శిష్యులను ఆదరించును: తన తండ్రి యింటిలో స్థలము సిద్ధపరచుటకు వెళ్లుచున్నాననియు, తండ్రియొద్దకు మార్గము తానేననియు చెప్పును. పరిశుద్ధాత్మను వాగ్దానము చేసి, తన సమాధానమును వారికి విడిచిపెట్టును.

items.title: ద్రాక్షావల్లియు కొమ్మలును
items.description: యేసు నిజమైన ద్రాక్షావల్లి, ఆయన శిష్యులు కొమ్మలు; వారు ఆయనయందు నిలిచి ఫలించవలెను. ఒకనినొకడు ప్రేమింపుడని ఆయన ఆజ్ఞాపించి, లోకము తనను ద్వేషించినట్టు వారిని కూడ ద్వేషించునని హెచ్చరించును.

items.title: ఆత్మ చేయు కార్యము
items.description: లోకమును ఒప్పించి, శిష్యులను సమస్త సత్యములోనికి నడిపించు సత్యస్వరూపియైన ఆత్మను యేసు వాగ్దానము చేయును. వారి దుఃఖము సంతోషముగా మారును: 'ధైర్యము తెచ్చుకొనుడి, నేను లోకమును జయించియున్నాను.'

items.title: యేసు తనవారికొరకు ప్రార్థించుట
items.description: యేసు ఆకాశమువైపు కన్నులెత్తి, తనకొరకును, తన శిష్యులకొరకును, వారి వాక్యమువలన విశ్వసించు వారందరికొరకును ప్రార్థించును. తానును తండ్రియు ఏకమైయున్నట్టు వారును ఏకమై యుండవలెనని ఆయన అడుగును.

items.title: అప్పగింపును బంధించుటయు
items.description: యూదా సైనికులను తోటలోనికి తీసికొనివచ్చును, యేసు బంధింపబడి అన్న, కయప, పిలాతుల యెదుటికి కొనిపోబడును. పేతురు మూడుసార్లు ఆయనను ఎరుగనని చెప్పును, కోడి కూయును.

items.title: సిలువ వేయుట
items.description: పిలాతు యేసును కొరడాలతో కొట్టించి, 'యూదుల రాజు' అను వ్రాత క్రింద గొల్గొతాలో సిలువ వేయుటకు అప్పగించును. యేసు తన తల్లిని యోహానుకు అప్పగించి, 'సమాప్తమైనది' అని చెప్పి, ఒక తోటలోని సమాధిలో పాతిపెట్టబడును.

items.title: ఖాళీ సమాధి
items.description: మగ్దలేనే మరియ రాయి దొర్లింపబడియుండుట చూచి, తోటలో లేచిన యేసును కలిసికొనును. తలుపులు మూయబడియుండగా యేసు తన శిష్యులకు కనబడును, సందేహించిన తోమా 'నా ప్రభువా, నా దేవా!' అని ఒప్పుకొనును.

items.title: సముద్రతీరమున అల్పాహారము
items.description: లేచిన యేసు గలిలయ సముద్రముమీద చేపలు పట్టుచున్న యేడుగురు శిష్యులను కలిసికొని, వారి వలను విస్తారమైన చేపలతో నింపును. తీరమున అల్పాహారము తరువాత, 'నీవు నన్ను ప్రేమించుచున్నావా?' అని మూడుసార్లు అడిగి, 'నా గొఱ్ఱెలను మేపుము' అని ఆజ్ఞాపించి పేతురును ఆయన తిరిగి నియమించును.

original.book_description: యోహాను సువార్త తన వేదాంత లోతు మరియు దేవుని శాశ్వతమైన వాక్యంగా యేసు గుర్తింపుపై తన ప్రత్యేక దృక్పథంతో ఇతర సువార్తల నుండి భిన్నంగా ఉంటుంది. యేసు క్రీస్తు అని పాఠకులు నమ్మడం కోసం వ్రాయబడిన యోహాను, యేసు దివ్య స్వభావాన్ని వెల్లడి చేసే ఏడు అద్భుత సంకేతాలను మరియు ఏడు 'నేనే' ప్రకటనలను ప్రదర్శిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 1
items.description: అబ్రాహాము నుండి యోసేపు వరకు యేసు క్రీస్తు వంశావళి, మరియు పరిశుద్ధాత్మ వలన మరియ అద్భుతమైన గర్భధారణ గురించి యోసేపుకు దేవదూత ప్రకటన.

items.title: Matthew 2
items.description: తూర్పు దేశపు జ్ఞానులు నక్షత్రాన్ని అనుసరించి నవజాత రాజును కనుగొంటారు. బాలుడిని చంపాలనే హేరోదు కుట్ర యోసేపును మరియమును ఐగుప్తుకు పారిపోయేలా చేస్తుంది.

items.title: Matthew 3
items.description: బాప్తిస్మమిచ్చు యోహాను అరణ్యంలో మారుమనస్సును ప్రకటిస్తూ యొర్దాను నదిలో యేసుకు బాప్తిస్మం ఇస్తాడు, అక్కడ దేవుని ఆత్మ పావురంలా దిగి వస్తుంది.

items.title: Matthew 4
items.description: యేసు నలభై రోజులు అరణ్యంలో అపవాది చేత శోధించబడి, ఆ తరువాత గలిలయలో తన బహిరంగ పరిచర్యను ప్రారంభించి, తన మొదటి శిష్యులను పిలుస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 5
items.description: యేసు ధన్యవచనాలను మరియు పరలోక రాజ్యపు ఉన్నతమైన నీతిని బోధిస్తూ, తన అనుచరులను లోకానికి ఉప్పుగా మరియు వెలుగుగా ఉండమని పిలుస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 6
items.title_vernacular: కొండ మీది ప్రసంగం: ప్రార్థన మరియు నమ్మకం
items.description: యేసు దానధర్మం, ప్రభువు ప్రార్థనతో సహా ప్రార్థన, ఉపవాసం గురించి బోధిస్తూ, భౌతిక అవసరాల గురించి చింతించకుండా దేవునిపై నమ్మకం ఉంచమని చెబుతాడు.

items.title: Matthew 7
items.title_vernacular: కొండ మీది ప్రసంగం: జ్ఞానవంతుడైన మరియు మూర్ఖుడైన నిర్మాత
items.description: యేసు ఇతరులను తీర్పు తీర్చడం, ఇరుకైన ద్వారం, అబద్ధ ప్రవక్తలను గుర్తించడం, మరియు బండ మీద మరియు ఇసుక మీద కట్టడం అనే ఉపమానం గురించి బోధిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 8
items.description: యేసు ఒక కుష్ఠరోగిని, శతాధిపతి సేవకుని, పేతురు అత్తను మరియు ఇతరులను స్వస్థపరుస్తాడు. తుఫానును శాంతపరచి, గదరలో దయ్యాలను వెళ్లగొడతాడు.

items.title: Matthew 9
items.description: యేసు ఒక పక్షవాతపు రోగిని స్వస్థపరచి, సుంకరి మత్తయిని పిలిచి, ఒక బాలికను మరణం నుండి లేపి, గుడ్డివారిని మూగవారిని స్వస్థపరుస్తాడు. జనసమూహాల మీద కనికరపడతాడు.

items.title: Matthew 10
items.description: యేసు తన పన్నెండు మంది అపొస్తలులను స్వస్థపరచే మరియు ప్రకటించే అధికారంతో పంపిస్తూ, హింసల గురించి హెచ్చరిస్తూ భయపడవద్దని ప్రోత్సహిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 11
items.description: బాప్తిస్మమిచ్చు యోహాను యేసు మెస్సీయా అయితే అడగడానికి దూతలను పంపిస్తాడు. యేసు యోహానును ప్రశంసించి, మారుమనస్సు పొందని పట్టణాలను గద్దించి, అలసిపోయిన వారికి విశ్రాంతి ఇస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 12
items.description: విశ్రాంతి దినాచారం గురించి పరిసయ్యులతో వివాదాలు, ఎండిపోయిన చెయ్యిగల మనిషి స్వస్థత, మరియు పరిశుద్ధాత్మకు విరోధంగా దూషణ గురించి యేసు హెచ్చరిక.

items.title: Matthew 13
items.description: యేసు ఉపమానాలలో బోధిస్తాడు: విత్తనం చల్లేవాడు, గురుగులు, ఆవగింజ, దాచిన ధనం, ముత్యం మరియు వల — దేవుని రాజ్య రహస్యాలను బయలుపరుస్తూ.

items.title: Matthew 14
items.title_vernacular: యోహాను మరణం మరియు ఐదు వేల మందికి భోజనం
items.description: హేరోదు బాప్తిస్మమిచ్చు యోహానును శిరచ్ఛేదం చేస్తాడు. యేసు ఐదు రొట్టెలు రెండు చేపలతో ఐదు వేల మందికి భోజనం పెట్టి, నీళ్ల మీద నడిచి శిష్యుల పడవ వద్దకు వస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 15
items.description: యేసు ఆచారపరమైన కడుగుడు గురించి పరిసయ్యుల సంప్రదాయాలను ప్రశ్నించి, కనానీయ స్త్రీ కుమార్తెను స్వస్థపరచి, నాలుగు వేల మందికి భోజనం పెడతాడు.

items.title: Matthew 16
items.description: పేతురు యేసును క్రీస్తుగా, జీవముగల దేవుని కుమారునిగా ప్రకటిస్తాడు. యేసు తన మరణం మరియు పునరుత్థానం గురించి ముందుగా చెప్పి, సిలువను ఎత్తుకోవడం గురించి బోధిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 17
items.description: యేసు పేతురు, యాకోబు మరియు యోహానుల ముందు కొండ మీద రూపాంతరం చెందుతాడు, మోషే మరియు ఏలీయాతో కనిపిస్తాడు. దేవుని స్వరం యేసును తన ప్రియ కుమారునిగా ప్రకటిస్తుంది.

items.title: Matthew 18
items.description: యేసు బాలుల వంటి వినయం ద్వారా రాజ్యంలో గొప్పతనం, తప్పిపోయిన గొర్రె ఉపమానం, సంఘ క్రమశిక్షణ, మరియు డెబ్బై ఏడు సార్లు క్షమించడం గురించి బోధిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 19
items.description: యేసు వివాహం మరియు విడాకుల గురించి బోధించి, పిల్లలను ఆశీర్వదించి, ధనవంతుడైన యువకునికి సమస్తం అమ్మి తనను అనుసరించమని సవాలు చేస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 20
items.description: వేర్వేరు గంటలలో నియమించబడి సమాన వేతనం పొందిన పనివారి ఉపమానం. యేసు మళ్ళీ తన మరణాన్ని ముందుగా చెప్పి, సేవ చేయడం ద్వారా గొప్పతనం వస్తుందని బోధిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 21
items.description: జనసమూహాలు 'హోసన్నా' అని కేకలు వేస్తుండగా యేసు గాడిద మీద యెరూషలేములో ప్రవేశిస్తాడు. దేవాలయాన్ని శుద్ధి చేసి, అంజూరపు చెట్టును శపించి, విశ్వాసం గురించి బోధిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 22
items.description: పెళ్లి విందు ఉపమానం. మతపెద్దలు పన్నులు, పునరుత్థానం మరియు గొప్ప ఆజ్ఞ గురించి ప్రశ్నలతో యేసును పరీక్షిస్తారు.

items.title: Matthew 23
items.description: యేసు శాస్త్రులు మరియు పరిసయ్యుల కపటత్వానికి ఏడు వినాశనాలను ప్రకటించి, దేవుని దూతలను తిరస్కరించిన యెరూషలేము గురించి విలపిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 24
items.description: యేసు దేవాలయ నాశనం, అంతిమ కాల సూచనలు మరియు మనుష్య కుమారుని రాకడ గురించి మాట్లాడుతాడు. తన అనుచరులను సిద్ధంగా ఉండమని హెచ్చరిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 25
items.description: పది కన్యల మరియు తలాంతుల ఉపమానాలు సిద్ధపాటును బోధిస్తాయి. యేసు కనికరం ఆధారంగా గొర్రెలను మేకల నుండి వేరు చేసే అంతిమ తీర్పును వర్ణిస్తాడు.

items.title: Matthew 26
items.description: యేసు తన శిష్యులతో పస్కా భోజనం పంచుకొని, గెత్సెమనేలో ప్రార్థించి, యూదాచే అప్పగించబడి, బంధించబడి, ప్రధాన యాజకుని ముందు విచారణకు నిలబెట్టబడతాడు.

items.title: Matthew 27
items.description: యేసు పిలాతు ముందు తేబడి, మరణశిక్ష విధించబడి, సైనికులచే ఎగతాళి చేయబడి, గొల్గొతాలో సిలువ వేయబడతాడు. యేసు మరణించి సమాధి చేయబడగా భూమి మీద చీకటి కమ్ముకొస్తుంది.

items.title: Matthew 28
items.description: స్త్రీలు ఖాళీ సమాధిని కనుగొని పునరుత్థానుడైన యేసును కలుసుకొంటారు. ఆయన తన శిష్యులకు సమస్త జనులను శిష్యులుగా చేయమని ఆజ్ఞాపిస్తాడు.

original.book_description: మత్తయి సువార్త యేసును వాగ్దానం చేయబడిన మెస్సీయగా మరియు ఇశ్రాయేలు రాజుగా ప్రదర్శిస్తుంది, అబ్రాహాము నుండి దావీదు ద్వారా ఆయన వంశావళిని గుర్తిస్తుంది. ప్రధానంగా యూదుల పాఠకుల కోసం వ్రాయబడిన మత్తయి, యేసు పాత నిబంధన ప్రవచనాలను ఎలా నెరవేర్చాడో నొక్కి చెప్తుంది.

items.title: The Spirit Descends and the Church is Born
items.description: పునరుత్థానుడైన యేసు పరలోకానికి ఆరోహణమై, పెంతెకొస్తు దినాన పరిశుద్ధాత్మ కుమ్మరించబడే సంఘం యొక్క ఆరంభాన్ని అనుభవించండి. పేతురు యొక్క ధైర్యమైన ప్రసంగం, తొలి విశ్వాసుల అద్భుత వృద్ధి, మరియు మొదటి వ్యతిరేక గుర్తులకు సాక్షిగా ఉండండి.

items.title: The Gospel Breaks Boundaries
items.description: యేసు సందేశం యెరూషలేమును దాటి వ్యాపించడం ప్రారంభమవుతుంది. ఫిలిప్పు సమరియను చేరుకుంటాడు, సౌలు దమస్కు మార్గంలో క్రీస్తును కలుసుకుంటాడు, మరియు పేతురు అన్యజాతీయుడైన కొర్నేలి వద్దకు నడిపించబడతాడు. సంఘం చెదరగొట్టబడినా బలపరచబడుతుంది, పౌలు తన మొదటి మిషనరీ యాత్రను ప్రారంభిస్తాడు.

items.title: Mission and Resistance
items.description: పౌలు మరియు బర్నబా ఆసియా, ఐరోపా అంతటా ఘర్షణ, హింస మరియు అద్భుతాలను ఎదుర్కొంటూ మిషనరీ యాత్రలు కొనసాగుతాయి. యెరూషలేము సభ ఒక కీలకమైన చర్చను పరిష్కరిస్తుంది, మరియు సువార్త యూదులకు మరియు అన్యజనులకు చేరుతుంది.

items.title: Bound Yet Unstoppable
items.description: యెరూషలేములో బంధించబడినా, పౌలు స్థిరంగా నిలుస్తాడు. విచారణలు, చెరసాలలు, ఓడ ప్రమాదం, మరియు రోము వరకు అతని చివరి ప్రయాణం ద్వారా ఆయనతో పాటు ప్రయాణించండి. సువార్తను ఆపలేము — సంకెళ్లలో కూడా.

original.book_description: The Acts of the Apostles is the New Testament's account of the birth and rapid expansion of the early Church. Picking up where the Gospel of Luke ends, Acts traces the outpouring of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost, the bold preaching of the apostles, the conversion of Saul of Tarsus into the apostle Paul, and the spread of the gospel from Jerusalem through Judea, Samaria, and across the Roman world to Rome itself. Acts shows how the message of Jesus broke through cultural, ethnic, and political boundaries to become a movement for all peoples.

sections.title: పరిచయం
sections.description: యుగయుగాలుగా మనుషులు అడుగుతూనే ఉన్నారు: ఈ లోకానికి — నా జీవితానికి — ఏదైనా ఉద్దేశం ఉందా? పరిచయం ఈ విశ్వవ్యాప్త ప్రశ్నను ముందుంచి, ఆదినుండి మాట్లాడుతూ వస్తున్న ఆ స్వరాన్ని చూపుతుంది — అది బైబిలు అనే గ్రంథంలో లిఖించబడింది.

items.title: Event 2
items.title_vernacular: ఆ స్వరం — బైబిలు అనే గ్రంథంలో శాశ్వతంగా లిఖించబడింది

sections.title: ఆదియందు
sections.description: కథ దేవునితో మొదలవుతుంది; ఆయన చేసిన ప్రతిదీ ఆయన స్వభావాన్ని ప్రతిబింబిస్తుంది. సృష్టి ఆయన శక్తిని, తత్వాన్ని వెల్లడిస్తుంది; ఆయన స్వరూపంలో చేయబడిన మానవుడు ఆయనను తెలుసుకోవడానికే సృజించబడ్డాడు.

sections.title: ఎంపిక
sections.description: తోటలో రెండు చెట్లు ఉన్నాయి; వాటితోపాటు నిజమైన ఎంపిక కూడా: దేవుని నమ్మడమా, సొంత దారిన పోవడమా. తెరవెనుక సాతాను తిరుగుబాటు కథలోని మహాసంఘర్షణకు రంగం సిద్ధం చేస్తుంది.

sections.title: ప్రాణాంతక వ్యాధి
sections.description: సర్పపు మోసానికి లోనై మొదటి నరుడు, నారి పతనమవుతారు; ప్రాణాంతక ఆత్మీయ వ్యాధి — పాపం — లోకంలో ప్రవేశిస్తుంది. అయినా తీర్పు గడియలోనే దేవుడు రక్షకుని గురించిన మొదటి వాగ్దానాన్ని ఇస్తాడు.

sections.title: వాగ్దానానికి నాంది
sections.description: పాపం వ్యాపించగా, హృదయంలో దుఃఖించిన దేవుడు మహాజలప్రళయంతో భూమిని శుద్ధి చేస్తాడు — అయితే నోవహును, అతని కుటుంబాన్ని కాపాడతాడు. బాబెలు వద్ద జనాంగాలు చెదరగొట్టబడి, దేవుని ఆశీర్వాద ప్రణాళికకు వేదిక సిద్ధమవుతుంది.

sections.title: ఆశీర్వదించబడి ఆశీర్వాదం కావడానికి
sections.description: దేవుడు అబ్రాహామును పిలిచి, అతని సంతానం ద్వారా భూమిపై సకల వంశాలు ఆశీర్వదించబడతాయని వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. కొండపై అబ్రాహాము తన కుమారుని అర్పించడం — దేవుడే ప్రత్యామ్నాయాన్ని సమకూర్చుతాడనే సజీవ చిత్రంగా నిలుస్తుంది.

sections.title: వాగ్దాన ప్రజలు
sections.description: ఇస్సాకు, యాకోబు, యోసేపుల ద్వారా వాగ్దానం సజీవంగా కొనసాగుతుంది — ఐగుప్తు దాస్యంలో సైతం. దేవుడు మోషేను సిద్ధపరచి, బలమైన హస్తంతో హెబ్రీ ప్రజలను బయటకు నడిపిస్తాడు.

sections.title: దేవుని మార్గాలలో నడవడానికి పిలుపు
sections.description: సీనాయి వద్ద దేవుడు ధర్మశాస్త్రాన్ని ఇస్తాడు — అది ఆయన పరిశుద్ధతను, ప్రజల అవసరాన్ని వెల్లడించే పవిత్ర అప్పగింత. ఆశీర్వాదం-బానిసత్వాల చక్రాలు ఏ న్యాయాధిపతి, ఏ రాజు కంటే గొప్ప రక్షకుని అవసరాన్ని సూచిస్తాయి.

sections.title: వాగ్దత్తుడు
sections.description: కాల సంపూర్ణతలో వాగ్దత్త రక్షకుడు జన్మిస్తాడు. యేసు పెరిగి, బాప్తిస్మం పొంది, అరణ్యంలో శోధకునిపై విజయం సాధిస్తాడు — తాను ఎవరో, ఎందుకు వచ్చాడో ప్రకటిస్తూ.

sections.title: యేసు పరిచర్య
sections.description: యేసు తన శిష్యులను పిలిచి అధికారంతో పరిచర్య చేస్తాడు — బోధిస్తాడు, స్వస్థపరుస్తాడు, పాపాలను క్షమిస్తాడు. ఆయన మాటలు, కార్యాలు ఒక ప్రశ్నను తప్పనిసరి చేస్తాయి: ఈ మనిషి ఎవరు?

sections.title: దేవుని ప్రేమ–న్యాయాల సంగమం
sections.description: యేసు తన లక్ష్యాన్ని ప్రకటించి, మతనాయకులను ఎదుర్కొంటాడు, శిష్యులతో చివరి గడియలు గడుపుతాడు. అన్యాయపు విచారణ గుండా ఆయన సిలువ వైపు స్వచ్ఛందంగా సాగుతాడు — అక్కడ దేవుని ప్రేమ, న్యాయం కలుసుకుంటాయి.

sections.title: ఆయన లేచాడు
sections.description: యేసును అరువు సమాధిలో ఉంచుతారు — కానీ మరణం ఆయనను బంధించలేకపోయింది. లేచి ఆయన తన అనుచరులకు కనబడి, వారి దుఃఖాన్ని చెక్కుచెదరని ఆశగా మారుస్తాడు.

sections.title: ఆయన అనుచరులు
sections.description: పరిశుద్ధాత్మ దిగివస్తాడు; యేసు అనుచరుల సమాజం జన్మిస్తుంది. యుగాల పొడవునా ఆయన కథ ప్రతి జనాంగానికీ వ్యాపించింది — అది నేటికీ రాయబడుతూనే ఉంది.

sections.title: ఆహ్వానం
sections.description: కథ మొదలైన చోటే ముగుస్తుంది: ఒక ప్రశ్నతో. రక్షకుడు వచ్చేశాడు; ఆయన ఆహ్వానం మీ కోసమే.

original.title: ఆశ
original.film_description: «ఆశ» బైబిలు కేంద్ర కథలో 80 నిమిషాల ప్రయాణం; అది 36 ఘట్టాలలో చెప్పబడింది: సృష్టి అద్భుతం, పతన విషాదం, అబ్రాహాముకు, మోషేకు దేవుడు ఇచ్చిన వాగ్దానాలు, వాగ్దత్త రక్షకుని రాక — యేసు జననం, పరిచర్య, మరణం, పునరుత్థానం. కథకుని శైలిలో నాటకీయ దృశ్యాలతో అల్లిన ఈ చిత్రం దేవుని వాగ్దాన సందేశాన్ని ప్రపంచవ్యాప్త ప్రేక్షకులకు చేర్చింది. నిర్మాణం: మార్స్ హిల్ ప్రొడక్షన్స్; మరిన్ని వివరాలు: thehopeproject.com.
original.shortDescription: సర్వమానవాళికి దేవుని వాగ్దాన కథ — సృష్టి నుండి క్రీస్తు వరకు బైబిలు మహాకథ, 36 ఘట్టాలలో. మార్స్ హిల్ ప్రొడక్షన్స్ సమర్పణ.
original.longDescription: «ఆశ» బైబిలు కేంద్ర కథలో 80 నిమిషాల ప్రయాణం; అది 36 ఘట్టాలలో చెప్పబడింది: సృష్టి అద్భుతం, పతన విషాదం, అబ్రాహాముకు, మోషేకు దేవుడు ఇచ్చిన వాగ్దానాలు, వాగ్దత్త రక్షకుని రాక — యేసు జననం, పరిచర్య, మరణం, పునరుత్థానం. కథకుని శైలిలో నాటకీయ దృశ్యాలతో అల్లిన ఈ చిత్రం దేవుని వాగ్దాన సందేశాన్ని ప్రపంచవ్యాప్త ప్రేక్షకులకు చేర్చింది. నిర్మాణం: మార్స్ హిల్ ప్రొడక్షన్స్; మరిన్ని వివరాలు: thehopeproject.com.

original.title: యేసును గూర్చిన నిజమైన కథ
original.film_description: get.revelationmedia.org/tel/salvationmobile ను సందర్శించండి.  iBIBLE యొక్క ప్రత్యేకమైన ఎపిసోడ్ అయిన యేసును గూర్చిన నిజమైన కథలో ఆయన ఏకైక కుమారుడైన యేసు ద్వారా దేవుడిచ్చు రక్షణ అను ఉచిత బహుమానమును గూర్చిన కథను చూడండి. యేసును గూర్చిన నిజమైన కథ, ఆదికాండము నుండి ప్రకటన గ్రంథము వరకు లోక రక్షకుడైన యేసు క్రీస్తు యొక్క నిజమైన వృత్తాంతమును తెలియజేస్తుంది. దేవుని రక్షణ కథ యొక్క విజువల్ మరియు ఆడియో ప్రదర్శన మానవాళి పాపములోనికి పడిపోవుట, తమను తాము రక్షించుకొనుటలో వారి యొక్క అసమర్థత, మానవాళిని విమోచించి పునరుద్ధరించుట కొరకు దేవుడు కలిగియున్న ప్రణాళికను బయలుపరుస్తుంది. మన కొరకు సిలువ మీద యేసు సాధించిన రక్షణ ప్రజలందరికీ పంచవలసిన సువార్త సందేశమైయున్నది. మీరు విశ్వాసముతో ప్రభువైన యేసు క్రీస్తును అంగీకరించి, ఆయన రక్షణ బహుమానమును స్వీకరించి, దేవుని బిడ్డ కావాలని కోరుతున్నారా?
original.shortDescription: The story of God's free gift of salvation through His Son Jesus — an iBIBLE special episode from RevelationMedia, presenting the true narrative of the Savior from Genesis to Revelation.
original.longDescription: The Real Story of Jesus is an iBIBLE special episode from RevelationMedia — a visual and audio presentation of God's story of salvation. It reveals mankind's fall into sin, our inability to save ourselves, and God's plan to redeem and restore us through His only Son. From Genesis to Revelation, it presents Jesus Christ, the Savior of the world, and the salvation He won on the cross — the Gospel message for all people, in the languages of the world. iBIBLE is a ministry of RevelationMedia; learn more at i.bible.
